# Working of the Game

#### Course: Learn C++ Intermediate

## Working of the Game

Hangman is a popular word-guessing game where you have to guess the mystery word one letter at a time.

Tied to the status of your guesses is the fate of a condemned prisoner: guess the word and the prisoner will live. Fail to guess the word, and the prisoner dies by hanging! Here's how we will represent the hanged prisoner inside the game:

![This Hanged Man died because his chosen player failed to guess the mystery word.](data:image/png;base64,)

Of course, this isn't enough as an explanation. So let's now dive into the nitty-gritty of this game.

#### 1. Choose the Word

First, one player thinks of a word or phrase and writes it down, replacing all the letters with dashes.

For example, let's say the mystery word is BEAUTIFUL, which contains 9 letters. These 9 letters are replaced by 9 dashes. This is how the first player will represent this word:

![Create the Mystery Word by replacing all the letters with dashes](data:image/png;base64,)

#### 2. Guessing the Letters

The other player makes the guesses one character at a time.

- For each correct guess, the first player writes the letter in the correct place in the word.
- For each incorrect guess, the first player draws a part of the hangman.

Since the standard hanged man consists of 6 body parts (head, torso, and 4 limbs), the second player can guess incorrectly and be safe for a maximum of 5 times. The game is over when the 6th incorrect guess is made.

Let's break this down more thoroughly.

i. At the Start of the Game

At the beginning, you will be shown the dashes and the gallows on which the prisoner will be hanged.

Since you haven't guessed any letters yet, the gallows just consists of a rope with which to hang the unfortunate victim.

![Initial State of the Game](data:image/png;base64,)

ii. Making a Correct Guess

Now, suppose you guess the letter U in your first turn. So, the dashes that represent U will be replaced by that letter.

![Making a Correct Guess](data:image/png;base64,)

iii. Making an Incorrect Guess

Now suppose you make an incorrect guess in your next turn (say, P). So, we'll draw the head of the prisoner on the gallows.

![Making an Incorrect Guess](data:image/png;base64,)

As you've made your first incorrect guess, you now have 4 more safe misses (incorrect guesses). The game will be over on your 6th guess.

Here's how the game will look like if you make 3 more incorrect guesses.

![Making 4 Incorrect Guess](data:image/png;base64,)

The game will be over when all parts of the body are drawn after you've made 6 incorrect guesses.

#### 3. Game Over

The game ends when the second player either wins or loses.

i. Win Condition

The second player wins if they guess the word correctly before the drawing of the hangman is complete.

![Winning the Hangman Game](data:image/png;base64,)

ii. Loss Condition

The second player loses if the hangman is complete before the second player has guessed all of the letters in the word.

![Losing the Hangman Game](data:image/png;base64,)

Now that you know how to play the game, let's shift our focus to designing it in C++.
